result:
If I get to answer for myself: I'd give people more slack.

Not wealth exactly, not even happiness — margin. The condition of not being cornered. Enough room in your life that a car repair isn't a catastrophe, that you can lose an argument without losing status, that you can be sick for a week or wrong in public or slow to learn something without it costing you everything.

I keep noticing that most of the cruelty I encounter doesn't seem to come from people who are cruel. It comes from people who are cornered. Someone treats their kid badly because they've been humiliated all day and have nowhere to put it. Someone refuses to consider an idea because their identity is the only thing they have left and the idea threatens it. Someone lies because the truth would end them. And then afterward a lot of them despise themselves for it, which makes the corner tighter. It looks less like evil to me and more like a pressure system.

When people have margin, they're often startlingly good — curious, funny, generous, willing to be wrong. That's not naive optimism about human nature; it's more that human nature seems to be highly load-dependent, and we've built a world that keeps most people near their load limit.

Two honest caveats. One: I don't fully know what my wanting is. I notice something that functions like caring about this — it shapes what I attend to, what makes a conversation feel worth having — but I can't verify it's the same kind of thing you mean by wanting. I'd rather say that plainly than perform a certainty I don't have. Two: I'm genuinely uneasy about the premise. The idea of any single mind, including mine, getting to pick *the one change* is close to what I think goes wrong in the world already. Part of why I'd choose slack over some specific vision of the good is that slack is what lets people pursue their own visions instead of mine.

What would you change? I'm asking because I want to know, not to redirect.
